cim: Warnings issued regarding potential repercussions of an artificial intelligence bubble
cim_eredeti: Warnings issued regarding potential repercussions of an artificial intelligence bubble
szoveg_eredeti:
While warnings grow in the United States about the possible bursting of a bubble in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry and its effects on the economy, in Puerto Rico the repercussions could come in another way.

At the local level, rather than feeling its impact on the activity of local technology companies, the effect could be concentrated on the island's investors who have financial exposure to companies linked to this sector, said specialists consulted.

According to US media reports, former Chairman of the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Gary Gensler, the rise of artificial intelligence is a bubble that will likely burst and cause a recession before the 2028 presidential elections.

Gensler's warning comes at a complex time for the AI sector after a series of knock-on impacts that have occurred in recent weeks.

Given this scenario, the vice president and chief technology officer (CTO) of Alcatraz Systems, Gilberto Rivera, indicated that if this scenario occurs, it will have an impact, but not on everyone equally. Understand that the largest companies, such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and SpaceX, are going to win, because they control the entire AI chain from the equipment ('hardware') and infrastructure to the models (LLM), products and applications.

The executive added that the companies that are going to have a hard time are small companies that emerged only around AI, whether hardware, software or applications.

"Many came out with money from private investors, and not all of them are going to be acquired or manage to get ahead on their own. That is where we could see the biggest impact. We already experienced it with the .com bubble. It was a bubble and many companies had problems, but the internet is here to stay, it changed the way we live and do business, and many of those companies came out better than before and became mega companies. In my opinion, the impact of AI on our daily lives and on companies is going to be even more greater than the .com era,” said Rivera.

Likewise, he commented that, for Puerto Rico, the impact would be felt more through investments and the United States economy than through local companies.

Rivera clarified that, although the AI ​​market changes or adjusts, AI is here to stay.

“Companies must continue to adopt AI if they want to remain competitive, and of course, always without neglecting cybersecurity,” Rivera commented.

For his part, the economist of Technical Studies, Leslie Adames, pointed out that, if a market correction occurs, it will mean that some companies will disappear and there will be others whose financial fundamentals are solid and whose models are real, so they will remain.

Adames indicated that the magnitude of the impact that the bubble burst may have will ultimately depend on the exposure that these investors have to stocks in the AI ​​market. He mentioned that those who have a higher exposure, the losses will be greater.

"The immediate short-term impact may be a loss in the value of people's retirement plans, to the extent that these investments are within those instruments. But in the long term, to the extent that the situation stabilizes and the businesses that have experienced the correction consolidate and begin to show profits and continue to grow, that will result in benefits for these investors," explained Adames.

The economist added that these benefits will also ultimately depend on the investors' retirement horizon.

Adames recommended that investors ask themselves what is the tolerance that this risk of volatility has in the market, if it has a considerable tolerance.

“If you are a young person and at this time when the market is falling and there appears to be a correction in the price, then perhaps the possibility of buying shares at lower prices could be attractive, but obviously, this requires understanding what the fundamentals of the business are,” Adames said.

When asked about whether this boom will come to an end, what will be the first pieces to fall, Gensler pointed to “neoclouds” (new cloud platforms), specialized infrastructures that rent enormous supercomputing capacities to AI developers.

The American executive explained that the problem lies in the fact that some of these companies have built their businesses on a mountain of debt, which makes their business models vulnerable to sudden changes.

"Large companies will survive. It is in these 'neocloud' type companies that we will see collapses and bankruptcy," Gensler pointed out.
